confirmed_findings: v1 hardware-SPI RAMRD and v2 historical-SIO RAMRD produced the same red=7c8000, green=007c80, blue=80007c, and pattern=7c8000 values under the current BSP runtime
therefore changing only the RAMRD observer was not sufficient to recover the historical all-solid-pass and three-pattern-mismatch oracle
historical fill_rect divided rectangles into at most 160x160 tiles and opened a window for every tile, while current Fault B opens one window for each complete rectangle

historical runtime initialized keyboard before LCD and did not initialize a PSRAM driver or audio DMA/PWM path; current runtime initializes LCD, probes PSRAM, initializes keyboard, starts audio, waits 250 ms, and then verifies LCD
the current log had audio irq=104 before LCD verification, so the one-microsecond SIO loop can be interrupted even though A1 proves this does not break a correct writer
historical SDK commit, compiler, binutils, CMake, generator, BIN hash, and retained UF2 are unavailable; current artifacts use SDK 2.2.0 commit a1438dff and GCC 13.2.1
historical and current coordinates, expected colours, mismatch calculation, SIO bit order, edge sequence, dummy counts, and SPI deinit/restore are equivalent
Fault B UART text window_cs=held_from_caset_through_ramwr is stale and conflicts with the canonical CS-separated source; it is not transaction evidence
